svg.title: Where the 16.7 ms goes: the town frame
svg.desc: Bars on a 0 to 60 ms scale for the town frame on route A: SH-4 13.6 ms split into transform, send and an unexplained rest; the TA fed beside the send with its vertex buffer 68 percent full; the PVR 15.9 ms split into the scene, the map pass, the shadow layer and an open remainder; no G2 work; the frame at about 55.6 ms, most of it waiting. Below: why the frame is longer than its work, the per-engine plan with the static bake split, and the console tests that would settle it.
svg.text: Where the 16.7 ms goes: the town frame, engine by engine
Route A (the PVR draws the map), map 256, all casters, 8 people and 4 hens; the HUD of 8 photos, one console, 2026-11-25 (wiki/limits/scenes.md).
Status: MEASURED our console · FACT a manual or our code · ESTIMATE our arithmetic or model · OPEN not known

2 Why is the frame longer than its work?
The model: the SH-4 builds frame N+1 while the PVR draws N, so a
frame is the larger side, 15.9 ms here: 60 fps on paper [ASSUMPTION].
The HUD says 18 fps. Two other frames disagree the same way:
· a3, another view: SH-4 22.6, PVR 16.0 ms, 25 fps [MEASURED, relayed]
· c4: frames 39.9 / 49.9 ms for 19 .. 27 ms of work, in steps 10.0 ms
apart [MEASURED PVR-094]
A wait that wakes on the 100 Hz scheduler tick fits c4's steps
[INFERENCE, three frames]. Cause [OPEN Q53, P10].
Until it is found, every "room left" figure is an upper bound.
3 With the bake split (gen 6.5 plan)
every line ESTIMATE; see static-bake-split
PVR
scene 7.1 + movers' map 0.4 (tile cut, PVR-092 c4's map) + mask
1.1 .. 4.1 (TOWN-054) = 8.6 .. 11.6 ms, + the patch layer [OPEN]
SH-4
transform 1.8 .. 2.9 + send 3.8 + static sun 0 + movers receiving
0.15 (TOWN-066) + ground re-read about 1 ms on re-centre frames
+ the bands' cut and the game's own work [OPEN]
G2 and the ARM
0 a frame; the ground rebake when the sun moves runs behind (S2 clock).
Reading it, and what to measure next
Neither side is over 16.7 ms on its own: SH-4 13.6, PVR 15.9. The frame is long because something waits, not because the work is too big.
The PVR is the tighter side: 0.8 ms under 60 fps with the full-screen shadow layer in. Route B's 7.1 ms says the scene itself is cheap.
The SH-4's known parts (transform and send) are about 5.6 .. 6.7 ms of its 13.6; the other half is not broken down.
1 ms is about 200,000 SH-4 cycles [FACT SH4-001]. Every ESTIMATE here is a measured unit cost times a count, not a frame timed in parts.
Console tests that would turn this page MEASURED
· time each wait apart in one frame: render done, vblank, the KOS tick, the list flips (P10, Q53; c4b counts vblanks per frame)
· split the SH-4 line: scene update, cull, casters, transform, send, HUD, each with the s2 clock pair
· route A's PVR with the map pass alone and the layer alone, to place the open 2.5 ms
· the TA's own time, if the HUD can read it (BUS-006)
